title: Introducing preemptible compute: the same compute, half the price
gist: Together AI is monetizing idle GPU capacity by selling preemptible Kubernetes nodes at a fixed 50 percent of on-demand pricing with a five-minute drain window, deliberately rejecting the variable spot-market pricing model used by hyperscalers. The five-minute reclamation window is calibrated so that even a 3.5TB checkpoint of a 321-billion-parameter model can be written to a parallel filesystem with headroom.

insights.claim: Together AI is pricing preemptible GPU nodes at a flat 50 percent of the on-demand rate, with the rate explicitly fixed rather than moving with a spot market — a deliberate divergence from hyperscaler spot pricing.
insights.speaker: Pavneet Ahluwalia, Varun Chakravarthy
insights.so_what: A predictable 50 percent discount, not auction pricing, is the neocloud's differentiation pitch against AWS/GCP spot — and it implies material spare GPU capacity to sell.
insights.quote: Preemptible nodes are billed at a flat 50% of the on-demand rate. The rate remains fixed rather than moving with a spot market.

insights.claim: Billing is metered every one to two minutes and charged sub-hourly, so a node that runs for 12 minutes is billed for approximately 12 minutes.
insights.speaker: Pavneet Ahluwalia, Varun Chakravarthy
insights.so_what: Minute-level GPU metering pushes the industry toward consumption billing and erodes the reserved-capacity revenue model.
insights.locator: Billing is sub-hourly, with usage metered

insights.claim: Preemptible capacity draws from unused inventory, so allocated capacity can stay below the customer's requested target when capacity is tight — the discount comes with no availability guarantee.
insights.speaker: Pavneet Ahluwalia, Varun Chakravarthy
insights.so_what: The offering is a utilization-smoothing mechanism for the provider; fill rates are an indirect read on how tight GPU supply actually is.
insights.locator: Because preemptible nodes draw from unused capacity

themes.theme: Five-minute drain as the design constraint

insights.claim: Reclamation follows a strict five-minute sequence: at T+0 the node is cordoned, a TogetherPreempted Kubernetes event fires and pods receive SIGTERM; workloads then have up to five minutes to checkpoint and exit before the node is removed at T+5:00.
insights.speaker: Pavneet Ahluwalia, Varun Chakravarthy
insights.so_what: The drain window is the contract that determines which workloads can migrate to cheap capacity — a five-minute standard is far more generous than typical cloud spot notice.
insights.locator: the cluster follows a five-minute drain

insights.claim: A full weight checkpoint for the 321-billion-parameter GLM5.3 Flash model is roughly 3.5TB and would take between 22 seconds and 4 minutes to write to a parallel filesystem even at degraded performance, leaving headroom inside the five-minute drain window.
insights.speaker: Pavneet Ahluwalia, Varun Chakravarthy
insights.so_what: Concrete sizing that shows even frontier-scale open models are checkpointable within interruption windows — parallel filesystem and storage throughput become the enabling infrastructure.

insights.claim: Recovery behavior, not workload size, is presented as the deciding factor for whether work belongs on preemptible capacity: anything chunked, checkpointed or retryable qualifies, while multi-day runs without checkpointing and strict-SLO serving with no fallback do not.
insights.speaker: Pavneet Ahluwalia, Varun Chakravarthy
insights.so_what: A clean decision rule for estimating what share of enterprise AI compute spend can migrate to discounted tiers.
insights.quote: The common thread: work that is chunked, checkpointed, or retryable.

insights.claim: Frameworks such as Ray Train and PyTorch Lightning already resume from the latest checkpoint without intervention, so the ecosystem tooling for interruption tolerance is presented as already in place.
insights.speaker: Pavneet Ahluwalia, Varun Chakravarthy
insights.so_what: Low switching friction means adoption of discounted capacity could be fast, compressing realized GPU pricing across the market.
insights.locator: Frameworks such as Ray Train and PyTorch Lightning

insights.claim: Preemptible nodes are not a separate cluster type but join existing clusters labeled together.ai/compute-class=preemptible, so interruptible workers run on discounted capacity while coordinators, login pods and serving replicas stay on standard nodes.
insights.speaker: Pavneet Ahluwalia, Varun Chakravarthy
insights.so_what: Mixed-class clusters lower the adoption barrier — customers blend cost tiers without re-architecting, which accelerates the blended-price decline.
insights.locator: Preemptible nodes are not a separate cluster type

insights.claim: Clusters must retain at least one standard node and nodes cannot be converted between compute types in place, with no minimum node lifetime guaranteed during the preview.
insights.speaker: Pavneet Ahluwalia, Varun Chakravarthy
insights.so_what: The constraints preserve a floor of guaranteed revenue per cluster — the discount tier is additive, not substitutive, for the provider.

insights.claim: Together AI says it runs several of its own internal research, dev/test and non-critical production workloads on preemptible clusters to use spare capacity across product teams.
insights.speaker: Pavneet Ahluwalia, Varun Chakravarthy
insights.so_what: Internal dogfooding suggests the primary business driver is raising fleet utilization rather than winning new customers.
insights.locator: Together has a strong culture dogfooding

insights.claim: The feature launches in public preview on Kubernetes clusters in all regions, with Slurm support, additional regions and in-place conversion between compute types named as the next roadmap items.
insights.speaker: Pavneet Ahluwalia, Varun Chakravarthy
insights.so_what: Slurm gaps signal the HPC/research segment is not yet addressable — a near-term expansion trigger to watch.
insights.locator: Preemptible compute is now in public preview
